claim: m20_ml_exit_probe.py::main() fails to unpack the (candles, bar_seconds) tuple that m20_exit_analysis.load_candles() returns — it assigns the whole 2-tuple to candles[sym] and then iterates over it as a list of candle dicts — so the script raises a TypeError and cannot run to completion on any resolvable symbol, meaning this committed M20 research probe (whose stated job is to decide whether an ML exit trigger is worth building) has never actually produced the analysis its own docstring describes.
evidence: Quoted lines: `if sym not in candles:\n            candles[sym] = load_candles(sym, ds_root)\n            cand_ts[sym] = [c[\"t\"] for c in candles[sym]]`. m20_exit_analysis.load_candles() is declared `-> Tuple[List[dict], float]` and does `return out, _infer_bar_seconds(out)` (or `return [], _DEFAULT_BAR_S`) — always a 2-tuple. Reproduced with a planted fixture: created a tiny market_raw/BTCUSDT/15m/*.jsonl file, called `load_candles("BTCUSDT", Path(ds_root))` (confirms it returns `(list, float)`), then executed the probe's exact two lines verbatim: `candles[sym] = load_candles(sym, Path(ds_root))` then `cand_ts[sym] = [c[\"t\"] for c in candles[sym]]` — output: `TypeError: list indices must be integers or slices, not str` (script: /tmp/claude-0/.../scratchpad/repro_ml_exit_probe.py). Compare to m20_exit_analysis.py's OWN main(), which correctly unpacks the same call as `c, bs = load_candles(s, ds_root)`.
expected: `candles[sym], _bar_seconds = load_candles(sym, ds_root)` (unpacking the tuple, as the sibling module's own main() does), then `cand_ts[sym] = [c["t"] for c in candles[sym]]` iterating the actual candle list.
actual: The whole (list, float) tuple is stored under candles[sym]; the very next line crashes with TypeError the first time any symbol in `shadow` resolves candle data, so main() never reaches the trade-join / bucket-and-print logic at all for a real dataset.
population: 1 occurrence (line 178); confirmed by direct repro with planted market_raw fixture data covering the exact code path main() executes for a resolvable symbol.
detector: No test currently exercises this: `grep -rl m20_ml_exit_probe tests/` finds only tests/test_check_research_index.py (checks the file is listed in a research index doc) and tests/ml/test_regime_score_semantics.py (tests the score-semantics module the probe imports, and only greps this file's SOURCE TEXT for the fixed max-proba bug it corrected — it never calls main() or load_candles against real data). A smoke test that runs main() end-to-end against a tiny planted candles+shadow-log+db fixture would catch this immediately (it crashes on the first iteration).
proposed_fix: In m20_ml_exit_probe.py main(), change `candles[sym] = load_candles(sym, ds_root)` to `candles[sym], _ = load_candles(sym, ds_root)` (bar_seconds is unused by this probe, which hardcodes BAR_S=900.0 separately — see the related low-severity granularity-mismatch note this same call site raises, since load_candles tries 15m/5m/1h/1d in order and the probe's own bar-index math assumes 900s regardless of which grain actually resolved).

claim: m20_banking_risk_adjusted.py::analyse()'s `dd_per_r` computation collapses a genuinely-measured zero drawdown delta (dD == 0.0, i.e. the cell measurably changed NO drawdown at all) into `None` (rendered as the em-dash '—', meaning 'undefined/unmeasured') instead of reporting the true value 0.0, because Python's `-0.0` is falsy and the code uses `x or None` to distinguish 'undefined' from a value — the exact inverse of the failure class this repo's own rules (and this very file's docstring) warn against ('never fabricate a comparison' / never render a measured quantity as unknown).
evidence: Quoted line: `"dd_per_r": _ratio(-(dD if dD is not None else 0.0) or None, -dR) if (dR is not None and dR < 0 and dD is not None) else None,`. Reproduced directly: `python3 -c "import sys; sys.path.insert(0,'scripts/research'); from m20_banking_risk_adjusted import _ratio; dR=-1.0; dD=0.0; cond=(dR is not None and dR<0 and dD is not None); print(_ratio(-(dD if dD is not None else 0.0) or None, -dR) if cond else None)"` prints `None` for a case where dR=-1.0 (the cell genuinely cost 1R of return) and dD=0.0 (the cell genuinely changed the book's drawdown by exactly zero) — a real, measured, unambiguous 'this trade cost return and bought nothing on drawdown' case, which should render as dd_per_r=0.00 (a bad trade-off) but instead renders identically to a case where the ratio is truly undefined (e.g. base has no drawdown). Confirmed the root cause with `bool(-0.0)` -> `False` in Python.
expected: A genuinely-measured dD == 0.0 should produce dd_per_r == 0.0 (a real, printable number: zero drawdown removed for the net_R surrendered), distinct from the actually-undefined cases the function already handles by returning None (dR is None, dD is None, or the outer `dR < 0` guard fails).
population: 1 occurrence (the dd_per_r field, computed once per IS/OOS window per cell for every verdicts.json this reporting-only tool reads); no test file exists for this module at all (`grep -rl m20_banking_risk_adjusted tests/` -> no matches).
detector: A unit test asserting `analyse()`'s dd_per_r for a fixture cell with dR<0 and dD==0.0 returns 0.0 rather than None would catch this; none exists today for this file.
proposed_fix: Replace the `or None` idiom, which conflates falsy-but-valid 0.0 with 'undefined', with an explicit conditional, e.g.: compute `neg_dd = -(dD if dD is not None else 0.0)` then set the numerator to `neg_dd` directly (never substituting None for a legitimate 0.0) since the None-ness of dD is already checked by the enclosing `if`; only fall back to None for the pre-existing undefined cases the outer condition already gates.
disposition: filed (docs/audits/code-audit-2026-09-27/CA-B03.findings.jsonl — below pipeline-filing threshold, no separate PI id)

claim: build_exit_panel.py writes the panel's `r` outcome column via a ternary that always evaluates to the same branch regardless of its condition (`X if False else None`), leaving confusing dead code that always assigns None.
evidence: Quoted line 414: `"r": exc.get("mfe_r") if False else None,  # r not computed here; excursions carry R`. `if False` is a literal that can never be true, so `exc.get("mfe_r")` is dead code that is computed-and-discarded every row; the column is unconditionally `None`. Confirmed by inspection; functionally harmless today (comment correctly states intent) but is exactly the kind of residue that silently starts doing something different if a future edit changes `False` to a real condition without noticing the branch was already dead, or if someone 'simplifies' it to just `exc.get('mfe_r')` believing the ternary was meaningful.
expected: The `r` column, which the panel manifest documents as an outcome column (`_OUTCOME_COLS` includes `"r"`), should either be genuinely computed (if a real R value is available) or the code should plainly state `"r": None` with no dead conditional.
actual: The line always assigns `None`, dressed up as a conditional, making a future reader (or editor) have to reason about a branch that can never execute.
detector: A linter rule flagging a literal `if False`/`if True` conditional (e.g. `flake8-simplify`'s SIM108-adjacent checks, or a simple `ruff` rule for constant-condition ternaries) would catch this on any future PR.
proposed_fix: Replace `"r": exc.get("mfe_r") if False else None,  # r not computed here; excursions carry R` with `"r": None,  # not computed here — excursions carry the R-equivalent outcomes (mfe_r/mae_r/giveback_r/...)`.
disposition: filed (docs/audits/code-audit-2026-09-27/CA-B03.findings.jsonl — below pipeline-filing threshold, no separate PI id)

location: scripts/research/component_edge_report.py:165-166 (fallback def contract_value_usd_for), triggered by the try/except at :114-126
evidence: Read of lines 109-176: `try: from src.web.api._clean_trades import ...; from src.runtime.local_pnl import contract_value_usd_for; _CLEAN_TRADES_OK = True; except Exception: _CLEAN_TRADES_OK = False` followed by a local stub `def contract_value_usd_for(symbol): return 1.0`. actual: The report proceeds normally and writes rCoverage/R values computed with contract_value_usd=1.0 with no per-report flag distinguishing this from the real computation; only the summary object (not persisted per report.json in a reader-visible way beyond the top-level build_reports() return) carries `clean_trades_helpers`.
population: 1 module; verified the fallback is currently unreachable in this repo (import succeeds) via direct python3 import check, so n=0 live-affected reports today
detector: A unit test that monkeypatches the src.web.api._clean_trades import to fail and asserts the resulting component_edge report either refuses (verdict=insufficient/no R claim) or stamps a visible degraded-R flag in every emitted report row.
proposed_fix: In the except branch, set a module-level DEGRADED_CONTRACT_VALUE = True and thread it into analyze_strategy()'s output (e.g. report['r_basis_degraded'] = not _CLEAN_TRADES_OK), and render it prominently in _render_md so nobody reads a degraded-R report as a normal one.

claim: scripts/ci/check_cost_model_single_owner.py's KNOWN_DUPLICATES comment (lines 62-64) falsely claims the 5 listed files 'now import execution_costs (to wire slippage/funding) and alias FEE_BPS_ROUNDTRIP to the owner -- no longer duplicates. Removed rather than left stale', while the dict on the very next lines still lists all 5 as registered literal '7.5' duplicates, and none of the 5 files actually import execution_costs or compute slippage/funding -- a direct comment-vs-field contradiction inside a guard whose entire purpose is to prevent exactly this kind of drift.
evidence: Read lines 61-70: comment reads 'checklist E3 (2026-09-21): these 6 now import execution_costs (to wire slippage/funding) and alias FEE_BPS_ROUNDTRIP to the owner -- no longer duplicates. claim: e38_regime_classification.py's `assert out["fixture_read"] is False` verifies nothing: the value it checks was hardcoded to False three lines above it, so the assertion can never fail and gives no real evidence that the committed backtest_candles.csv fixture was not read.
location: scripts/research/e38_regime_classification.py:421-433 (dict literal sets fixture_read at ~426, assert at 432-433)
evidence: grep -n FIXTURE scripts/research/e38_regime_classification.py shows FIXTURE (data/backtest_candles.csv) is referenced only at its definition (line 49) and inside the assert's json.dumps string-search (line 433) -- it is never opened or read anywhere in the module. The first clause of the assert, `out['fixture_read'] is False`, is a tautology against a literal set a few lines earlier in the same dict, so it can never catch a regression that actually started reading the fixture (e.g. a future edit to fetch_daily that adds a fallback read). The second clause (searching provenance values for the path string) is a real but narrow check that would only catch the fixture path leaking into the small provenance dict, not an actual read of the file elsewhere in analyse_leg/load_trades.
expected: A self-check meant to guarantee 'the fixture is never read' should assert something derived from actual I/O (e.g. a monkeypatched/tracked open() call, or a fixture mtime/access check), not re-assert a hardcoded literal against itself.
actual: The assertion is vacuous for its first clause and only weakly protective for its second; today it happens to be harmless because nothing in the module calls open() on FIXTURE at all, so there is no live bug -- only a self-check that would not catch one if introduced later.
population: 1 module, 1 assert statement; verified by full-file grep for every reference to the FIXTURE constant (2 occurrences total, neither an open/read call)
detector: A CI guard could statically forbid `assert <var> is <literal>` where <var> was itself just set to that literal in the same function -- or, more simply, replace the check with an actual read-tracking wrapper around fetch_daily's file access and assert on that trace instead.
proposed_fix: Replace the vacuous clause with a real guard, e.g. wrap the whole analyse-legs loop so any os.path access to FIXTURE increments a counter (via unittest.mock.patch or a small sentinel Path subclass) and assert that counter is 0, or simply delete the dead `out['fixture_read'] = False` self-referential check and rely on the (already correct) fact that fetch_daily() only ever calls fetch_klines_binance_vision.
disposition: filed (docs/audits/code-audit-2026-09-27/CA-B03.findings.jsonl — below pipeline-filing threshold, no separate PI id)

expected: The --tp-cap-pct help text in m20_flip_replay_sweep.py should describe the fix as historical (as the surrounding paragraphs already do: 'this driver called base_args POSITIONALLY... EVERY regime_flip_exit cell... was therefore replayed against a book with NO take-profit') and either drop the now-false claim about the rollup's current pin, or state that the sentinel WAS pinned until 2026-08-16 when it was removed once a live-parity sweep landed.
